messages:
PagerDuty Bot: 🔴 ALERT 1769123456 - elevated 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate in us-east-1 (threshold 2% -> current 7%). Alerts: https://alerts.redwood.example/1769123456
Maya: acked, I'm oncall. starting triage — checking dashboards + recent deploys.
Ops Bot: Automated summary: 5xx spike started at 2026-03-15T01:25:10Z, error_type: upstream_timeout | gateway_502, affected service: gateway-proxy (frontdoor), p50 latency +120ms. Recent deploys: none in last 2 hours.
Sanjay: seeing a lot of 502s from gateway-proxy -> inference-backend. Traces for those requests are sparse, lots of missing spanids.
Maya: that smells like sampling/drop of trace headers. do we have request-id propagation enabled? any LB/ingress changes?
Eli: quick check — envoy sidecar is propagating x-request-id, but our tracing agent in the gateway is returning 204 on span creation intermittently. debug logs are sparse because production sampling is low.
Priya: customer impact? any high-tier customers hitting errors?
Ops Bot: Top affected customers by errors: acme-inc (30% of errors), beta-prod (12%), unknown retries from mobile clients. No PagerDuty incidents from customers yet.
Maya: plan: (1) ramp sampling for gateway traces to 100% for next 30m to capture root cause, (2) enable temporary request-id header passthrough on the edge, (3) add short-lived debug logs on gateway-proxy (info->debug) for key code paths.
Sanjay: I can flip sampling. running patch now.
Sanjay: ```bash
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/gateway-proxy TRACING_SAMPLING=1.0
# or for daemonset agent: curl -X POST http://tracing-agent:9411/admin/sampling?rate=1.0
```
Eli: toggled logging to debug on gateway-proxy replicas 3/3. watch logs: `kubectl logs -f deploy/gateway-proxy -c gateway`
Carlos: I'm seeing increased log volume; storage alerts may trigger. i'll stream debug logs into a temporary s3 bucket and set TTL 24h. starting job now.
Carlos: ```bash
kubectl exec -n prod job/log-streamer -- /bin/sh -c "tail -n +1 /var/log/gateway/*.log | aws s3 cp - s3://redwood-debug/gateway/1769123456-$(date -u +%s).log" &
```
Maya: good. also we need to patch the edge to force `x-request-id` passthrough instead of generating new ones. Priya can you prepare the envoy filter?
Priya: prepping envoy filter change, small inline filter to preserve incoming `x-request-id` and inject if missing. will patch canary first.```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  envoy_filter: |
    - name: preserve-x-request-id
      typed_config:
        "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.header_to_metadata.v3.Config
        request_rules:
        - header: x-request-id
          on_header_present: { metadata_namespace: envoy.lb, key: request_id }
```
Maya: canary applied to 1 pod — monitoring for errors.
Ops Bot: Note: traces now have spanids for ~35% of new errors after sampling flip. still some requests with no spans.
Sanjay: digging into gateway logs — getting repeated `upstream connect timeout` to inference-backend-host:9000 around the time of spike. tail of logs: ```
[2026-03-15T01:27:12Z] ERROR gateway: upstream connect timeout to inference-backend-host:9000 request_id=abc123
[2026-03-15T01:27:12Z] ERROR gateway: upstream response 502 after 10s request_id=abc123
```
Eli: looks like backend is timing out under specific payload shapes — maybe KV-cache miss or long seq length. Can we temporarily increase backend concurrency or extend upstream timeout as a stopgap?
Carlos: I can apply a routing-level retry/fallback to a lower-capacity model pool to reduce errors for high-latency requests. small config patch.
Priya: applied fallback route to model-quantized-pool for requests tagged `seq_len>2048` (canary). monitoring.
Maya: update: customer impact currently ~12% of requests get 5xx, but high errors concentrated to long-context requests and specific customer (acme-inc) traffic. outreach: I'll loop in success to notify acme support.
Sanjay: while we have sampling high, I'm seeing correlation: requests that hit an internal cache miss then trigger a heavy recompute path cause backend latency >8s -> gateway 502. we should enable an internal metric to surface `kv_cache_miss` count. logging doesn't currently emit that metric (observability gap).
Eli: quick hack: add a short-lived metric emission from gateway when it receives a `kv-miss` via statsd `gateway.kv.miss:1|c`. patching now.
Eli: ```python
# in gateway handler
if is_kv_miss():
    statsd.increment('gateway.kv.miss')
```
Maya: thanks. also create an incident ticket with summary + actions for handoff to next oncall.
Maya: Handoff summary for next oncall (timestamp 1769123810):
- Current status: 5xx spike partially mitigated by sampling, debug logs and temporary route fallback. Error rate down from 7% -> 3.6% after fallback.
- Customer impact: acme-inc seeing highest error share, internal probe shows failures correlated with long-context generation.
- Actions taken: increased trace sampling, enabled x-request-id passthrough, debug logging streaming to s3, applied fallback to quantized model pool for long requests, emitted temporary `gateway.kv.miss` metric.
- Open follow-ups: add permanent kv-miss metric, investigate inference-backend queueing, implement smarter routing for long-context requests, storage cleanup for debug logs (TTL), roll back debug logging once stable.
Maya: @Sanjay @Eli please add any outstanding playbook steps to the ticket. I'll hand this to @Carlos for night shift monitoring in 20m. :white_check_mark:
Carlos: taking handoff. I'll keep sampling on for 30m then drop to 10% if error rate stays <4%. I'll also keep the S3 stream running and set an alert for log volume.
Priya: I'll open a PR to add the `x-request-id` enforce/preserve rule to our common envoy filters and include unit tests.
Maya: thanks all. closing this thread for now — continue updates in the incident ticket and #incidents-status if anything regresses. :lock:
